text:
Maria: heads-up — this morning's shoulder (05:30-07:30 UTC) showed an unusual warmup waste pattern on us-east-dedicated pool. token/sec looks normal, but GPU-hours spiked ~8h above forecast.
Alex: saw that too. timeline? was it gradual or a sudden contraction/expansion?
Maria: sudden. around 05:42 we had a 30% jump in concurrent requests for ~3m, autoscaler spun up 4 extra nodes, KV cache cold, warmup tokens went through the roof.
Kevin: rough numbers from metrics:
- baseline tokens/s (steady): ~120k
- shoulder baseline tokens/s: ~40k
- 05:42 spike peak tokens/s: ~200k for 3m
- concurrent requests baseline: 800 -> spike 2400
- estimated warmup wasted tokens: ~1.1M tokens (12% of spike traffic)
Julia: 1.1M wasted tokens -> how does that map to GPU-hours? I did a quick back-of-envelope: ~8 GPU-hours across the pool (because warmup is KV+longer decode per token).
Henry: cost hit then. That aligns with the billing anomaly I flagged for us-east-dedicated yesterday.
sre-bot: ALERT: autoscale-trigger/us-east-dedicated at 2026-02-11T05:42:11Z — scale +4. Reason: concurrent_requests > 2000 for 120s
Maria: root cause likely twofold: small burst from a large customer (no rate limiting) + our scale-up policy that doesn't pre-warm variant replicas. The policy waits for node readiness, then routes real traffic immediately instead of warmup prefills.
Alex: Does the runtime support prefill/standby replica warmup? We have a prefilling path but it's opt-in per model and not enabled for the new opt-quant variants.
Kevin: correct. Prefill only enabled for redwood/opt-3b-v2 in hosted, not for most dedicated model variants. Also, warmup cost per token is ~1.7x vs steady-state because memory copies + KV initialization.
Julia: Quick mitigation ideas:
- temporary conservative headroom (30%) for shoulder windows
- enable prefill for the high-risk models in dedicated pools
- soft rate-limit the largest customer during shoulder windows
- add a short pre-warm ping path (small synthetic prefix requests) to newly provisioned nodes
Maria: I'd add: change scale policy to stagger rollout (route small percentage to new nodes first) — gives time for KV to populate without dumping customer traffic on cold cache.
Henry: tradeoffs: more standing capacity vs wasted GPU-hours. Need numbers for the 30% headroom ask.
Alex: rough calc: for us-east-dedicated shoulder window (2h) with avg 40k tokens/s -> 288M tokens. 30% headroom adds ~86M tokens capacity; if that headroom is idle it's ~6 GPU-hours/day. But compared to 8 GPU-hours lost in today's spike, headroom could be cheaper if it avoids scale churn.
Kevin: Also consider dynamic short-lived prefill pods that accept only prefix traffic and then hand off; cheaper than full node because they can run smaller batch sizes/quantized profiles.
Julia: Ops plan for today:
1) enable prefill for the two largest models in us-east-dedicated (toggle + monitor)
2) add a conservative 20% headroom for next 48h in peak-shift windows
3) patch autoscaler to stagger node routing by 10s intervals (canary traffic 5%)
4) contact the large customer about burst smoothing / rate-limit agreements
Maria: I'll open a PR for the autoscaler change.
Henry: I'll run cost delta sims comparing 20% vs 30% headroom and send results by EOD.
Alex: I'll get a quick dashboard with warmup-token metric (tokens labeled warmup:true) and annotate today's incident.
sre-bot: NOTE: incident ticket created — INC-4921 — "us-east shoulder warmup waste". Assigned: eng-infra.
Kevin: one more ask — add a small synthetic warmup sampler that runs a cheap batch every 30s for newly-started nodes for the next 24h (feature-flagged). Should shave 60-80% of warmup penalty per node.
Maria: agreed. keep it feature-flagged, we can revert if we see noise.
Julia: sounds good. TL;DR: warmup leak cost ~8 GPU-hours today due to sudden spike; mitigations: prefill, modest headroom, stagger rollout, synthetic pre-warm. Next steps assigned.
Alex: nice. postmortem note: we should also add an automated alert for warmup-token ratio > 10% for 5m.
Maria: adding that to the incident ticket now. :thumbsup:
Henry: thanks team — will track cost numbers and loop back in the daily at 14:00 UTC.
